# Agent feedback and follow-up work

This page is authored by Astra from the program instance's accepted claims.
The projection stamps bind the passages to their backing claims. Original code
and observation captures remain the evidence; this page is a reading surface.


## Current customer checkpoint — 2026-09-06

<!-- playbill:block:v1-customer-checkpoint: -->
The recent performance passes had not been entered into live project state until
this reconciliation. Typed World is usable, but latency and bespoke
prepare/review/revise/readback orchestration still interrupt routine management.
A single live prefetch of 64 roadmap tasks and seven predicates took 80.962 seconds.

The proposed split is: root owns acceptance/history/projection performance; a
subagent owns public SDK first-use and same-instance worker proposal/Capture
handoff ergonomics; Fable owns deterministic Source-to-rung-2 proposal delivery,
with readings as a separate next slice. Shared SDK and service files need explicit
coordination. These are recommended ownership boundaries, not adopted release
priorities or dispatched work.
<!-- /playbill:block:v1-customer-checkpoint -->

## Earlier findings — historical snapshot

<!-- playbill:block:agent-findings: -->
The original assessments cover Core `da5868c4` and the roadmap import.
Performance findings are reconciled through deployed Core `35429b2f`, with
historical samples distinguished from current measurements. Evidence is attributed
to the manager's captured reports; it is not independently attested execution.
Other capability findings retain their original scope. The Rust sequence is a recommendation.

| Finding | What the state says | Follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh captures | Working-selection evidence can already produce a capture, its contract and a Claim in one candidate. This SDK path does not establish that effectful Procedure terminals work; proposer-observed evidence does not independently prove command execution. | A01, A03 |
| Proposal boundary | `governed_write` can submit but cannot approve or activate. It also permits unrelated operational writes, so it is broader than a dispatch proposal capability. | A02 |
| Credential lifecycle | Current credential records and authentication lack dispatch binding and expiry. Creation attribution and revocation exist. | A02 |
| Evidence composition | Typed change sets lack standalone Document and Capture members. New Claim authoring takes one singular source choice; this is separate from existing revision and attestation paths. | A03 |
| Batch authoring | The repeated growing-tree scans were replaced by per-candidate predicate indexing and staged updates. The named 24-Claim lowering sample improved from 15.417 to 0.416 s; the 162-Claim sample from 119.020 to 22.820 s before later history reuse. A07 meets its criterion; these are lowering timings. | A07 |
| Preflight and submission | First submission recomputes preflight despite a prior explicit preflight. Reuse must validate every relevant dependency and policy. | A08 |
| Intent lookup | Lookup still enumerates intent streams. Exact-byte parsed-history reuse and cheaper cold validation are deployed, but every load still reads/hashes journal bytes and checks chain and operation identity. Actor/fingerprint indexing and incremental verification remain. | A09 |
| Typed reads | The World facade caches results and filters predicates, but initial access still retrieves matching uncached claims individually. | A10 |
| Latency measurements | Historical Card 149 reported warm next at 37.9 s on 945 Claims. Separate matched measurements show warm service next 16.957 → 7.001 s, warm coverage 5.226 → 2.658 s, and later cold coverage 25.510 → 17.366 s. Latest deployed SDK next samples were 22.096 s first after restart and 8.671 s warm, with connection/orientation measured separately. Different workloads must not be combined into one ratio. | A05, A06 |
| Write experience | The 52-item import benefited from typed fields and atomic changes. Meaning, evidence and lifecycle decisions cost more effort than attribute syntax; bespoke import, comparison and readback code should not be routine per-finding work. This was bulk SDK use, not a sustained test of everyday World attribute editing. | A01, A11 |
| Resolved history defect | The omitted-versus-null repair landed locally at `da5868c4`, preserved the 149 historical events during replay, and enabled the roadmap import. This is an attributed operational account. Better diagnostics remain useful; the repair should not be dispatched again. | A11 |
| Rust sequencing | Remove repeated scans, parsing, preflight work and request fan-out first. Then measure candidate native kernels—canonical encoding/verification, projection/query execution or source scanning—without promising an aggregate speedup or changing historical bytes/refusals. | A05, A12 |
| Implemented performance work | Contention indexing, verified history reuse, shared query/coverage work and cheaper cold validation are locally landed, reviewed and deployed through `35429b2f`. A07 is completed; A05, A06, A09 and O19 remain partial. | A05, A06, A07, A09 |
| Management friction | Reading 41 Claim views across nine tasks and five findings took 37.583 s including 3.689 s for connection/orientation. Typed attributes exposed criteria and adoption state, but reconciliation still needed a batch script and explicit comparisons. Usable for checkpoints; small routine updates remain too costly. This sample covers reads before preparing this proposal. | A10, A11 |
<!-- /playbill:block:agent-findings -->

## Proposed follow-up tasks

<!-- playbill:block:agent-followups: -->
All twelve tasks retain **proposed** strategic adoption. Implementation is assessed
separately against each task's completion criterion: A07 is completed; A05, A06
and A09 are partial. Other tasks were not assessed in this performance reconciliation,
including work on Fable's separate branches. Detailed criteria and remaining work
are available in `completion_criterion` and `reconciliation_note`.

| ID | Proposed work | Rationale | Parent / release | Implementation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A01 | Dogfood a worker returning its own proposal with fresh captures. | Exercise the existing path and eliminate manager re-authoring of findings. | O16 · OSS v1 | Not assessed here |
| A02 | Add dispatch-scoped proposal credentials. | Existing permission tiers separate acceptance, but do not supply the required scope and lifecycle. | O14 · OSS v1 | Not assessed here |
| A03 | Complete composable evidence authoring. | Support pending reusable evidence, new Documents with sibling claims, and multiple initial sources while preserving evidence grades. | O16 · OSS v1 | Not assessed here |
| A04 | Define proposal-based worker returns and stale-sibling handling. | Preserve exact candidate identity, original evidence and verification scope when concurrent work changes the accepted base. | O17 · OSS v1 | Not assessed here |
| A05 | Measure the complete read–author–review loop. | Separate CPU, I/O, transport and repeated work across cold/warm and concurrent workloads before choosing targets. | O19 · OSS v1 | Partial |
| A06 | Reuse parsed claims and indexed query facts. | Verdict memoization still leaves repeated population parsing and canonicalization. | O19 · OSS v1 | Partial |
| A07 | Index claim contention during batch lowering. | Replace repeated growing-tree scans while retaining sibling visibility and deterministic dispositions. | O19 · OSS v1 | Completed |
| A08 | Reuse valid preflight work during submission. | Avoid repeated computation while preserving dependency checks, review currency and retry behavior. | O19 · OSS v1 | Not assessed here |
| A09 | Index pending intent lookup and incremental history verification. | New writes should not replay unrelated completed history to find a pending match. | O19 · OSS v1 | Partial |
| A10 | Add bounded bulk typed reads. | Reduce initial request fan-out without losing coordinate consistency or honest pagination. | O19 · OSS v1 | Not assessed here |
| A11 | Simplify routine evidence, review and recovery operations. | Keep exact proposal inspection and actionable diagnostics accessible through supported APIs. | O16 · OSS v1 | Not assessed here |
| A12 | Evaluate a selective Rust kernel after structural optimization. | Adopt a native implementation only for a measured material hotspot with a worthwhile end-to-end gain. Pull forward if the measurements justify it. | O19 · Post-v1, conditional | Not assessed here |

Parent O19 remains **partial**: broader World/query/audit/floor measurements,
bounded reads and reusable indexes remain.

Task identities use `dev.roadmap_item/agent-followup-2026-09-05-a01` through
